raids.name: Barrow Deeps
raids.location: Mount Hyjal; connected approaches via Winterspring and Blackmaw Hold
raids.note: Plan your group and travel route.

raids.name: Hyjal Summit
raids.note: Agree assignments and supply expectations with your raid.

raids.name: Onyxia’s Lair
raids.note: Every player carries Drakefire Amulet in their inventory. Blizzard recommends fire resistance preparation.

onyxiaHorde: Begin with Goretooth in Kargath, Badlands.
Complete Warlord’s Command in Lower Blackrock Spire.
Report to Eitrigg and Thrall in Orgrimmar.
Defeat Rend for For the Horde!
Meet Rexxar, then Myranda in Western Plaguelands.
Gather dragonspawn eyes and use the disguise for Emberstrife.
Complete the four named-dragon skull tests.
Return via Rexxar and defeat Drakkisath in Upper Blackrock Spire.
Claim the Drakefire Amulet and carry it to the raid.
progression.raidNote: All three raids are announced for December 9. Weekly resets are the current plan. Follow current encounter instructions rather than importing an old raid script.

professions.name: Engineering
professions.recommendation: A practical PvP project if you enjoy planning and funding situational tools. Verify each gadget’s restrictions.

professions.name: Mining
professions.recommendation: Pairs naturally with Engineering and provides materials to sell while leveling.

professions.name: Herbalism
professions.recommendation: Choose it to supply Alchemy or support a gathering economy.
professions.camping: Incense Candle offers an Intellect buff, exclusive with Arcane Intellect.

professions.name: Alchemy
professions.recommendation: Useful for supplying yourself and your group; do not assume profitable recipes before checking demand.
professions.camping: Mana Well supports mana users and is exclusive with Blessing of Wisdom.

professions.name: Skinning
professions.recommendation: An accessible leveling economy that pairs with Leatherworking.
professions.camping: Camp Chair offers 2% critical chance, exclusive with Moonkin Aura.

professions.name: Leatherworking
professions.recommendation: Inspect discovered recipes against your actual gear; crafted does not automatically mean best.
professions.camping: Camp Tent provides rested XP up to 5% of a level.

professions.name: Enchanting
professions.recommendation: A long-term supply and trading choice. Price the recipe and materials before investing.
professions.camping: Enchanted Lute supplies a Mark of the Wild alternative.

professions.name: Blacksmithing
professions.recommendation: Consider it for a specific verified recipe or a crafting goal, rather than a generic Rogue requirement.
professions.camping: Sharpening Wheel grants Strength, exclusive with Strength of Earth.

professions.name: Tailoring
professions.recommendation: Useful if bags and trading suit your plans; it is not a direct leather-gearing route.
professions.camping: Faction Banner grants Spirit, exclusive with Divine Spirit.

secondaries.name: First Aid
secondaries.recommendation: Keep bandages and a safe healing opportunity in your field plan.
secondaries.camping: First Aid Kit grants level-scaled Stamina, exclusive with Fortitude.

secondaries.name: Cooking
secondaries.recommendation: Carry food and establish camps when the area is secure.
secondaries.camping: Basic Campfire supports three contributed features initially.

secondaries.name: Fishing
secondaries.recommendation: Supplies ingredients and a useful group camp feature.
secondaries.camping: Fishing Bowl grants 8% stats, exclusive with Kings.

progression.campingNote: Two primary professions and all three secondaries are available. One feature per player; sit or craft for one minute. Features share a one-hour cooldown. Place camps away from exposed PvP traffic.

supplies.name: Thistle Tea
supplies.recommendation: Use while low enough to avoid wasting the restoration. Check shared cooldowns in your client.
supplies.sourceNote: Forever tooltip inspected and page opened.

supplies.name: Free Action Potion
supplies.effect: 30 seconds of stun and movement-impairing immunity; does not remove effects already active; two-minute cooldown.
supplies.recommendation: A preparation tool, not a reactive answer after you are already controlled.
supplies.sourceNote: Forever tooltip inspected and page opened. No immunity to every possible mechanic is claimed.

supplies.recommendation: A new slot option to price against how long you expect to keep the necklace.
supplies.sourceNote: Indexed Forever spell record inspected; direct open required JavaScript.

supplies.effect: +8% movement speed; formula record requires Enchanting 280.

matchups.name: Warrior
matchups.open: Approach with a control plan and a clear retreat. Avoid trading into an opponent who already has support.
matchups.respond: Separate your damage window from theirs; use terrain and control rather than standing still through their offensive abilities.
matchups.reset: Create distance before you are forced into a last-second escape. Reassess any bleed and nearby reinforcements.
matchups.warning: Absorption no longer prevents Warrior Rage generation. Old assumptions about fighting a shielded Warrior can mislead.
matchups.confirmedContext: Developer overview changes Rage generation through absorption.

matchups.name: Paladin
matchups.open: Scout active defenses and nearby allies. Begin with enough Energy to pressure while retaining an interrupt or control response.
matchups.respond: Track defensive cooldowns and choose a new damage window after protection ends. Commit Kick to a meaningful cast you can reach.
matchups.reset: Use a defensive pause to recover or leave instead of spending every cooldown into protection.
matchups.warning: Do not treat every Paladin as an old Classic Retribution build; Holy damage and healing options differ.
matchups.confirmedContext: Forever adds baseline Holy Strike and revised Holy, Protection and Retribution tools.

matchups.name: Hunter
matchups.open: Inspect the pet, trap location and terrain before committing. Secure your approach rather than chasing across open ground.
matchups.respond: Stay alert for traps placed during combat. Use cover and control to reduce free ranged attacks while closing.
matchups.reset: Leave along a route that breaks sight and accounts for the pet. Do not run back through an obvious trap.
matchups.warning: Forever Hunters can trap in combat. Pet family tools differ, so identify the actual pet.
matchups.confirmedContext: Developer overview confirms in-combat traps and distinct pet-family abilities.

matchups.name: Rogue
matchups.open: Scout likely approaches and wait for a favorable reveal. Keep a response to the opposing opener instead of spending everything immediately.
matchups.respond: Track their escape and control choices. Pool Energy when a brief pause allows a stronger follow-up.
matchups.reset: Move away from the last contact point and check harmful effects before attempting to disappear.
matchups.warning: Damage-over-time and area effects can spoil a control reset. Opponent weapon and talent choices matter.
matchups.confirmedContext: Forever retains Stealth control and expands Rogue weapon options; current tuning changes its talents.

matchups.name: Priest
matchups.open: Look for a route that keeps you close without exposing you to allies. Plan a healing-interrupt window rather than a blind damage race.
matchups.respond: Save Will of the Forsaken for an eligible control effect at a useful moment; keep Kick for a cast that matters.
matchups.reset: Break sight and stop feeding an unfavorable exchange. Review active damage-over-time effects before a new approach.
matchups.warning: Fear Ward and Devouring Plague are available to every Priest at level 20; race alone no longer identifies access.
matchups.confirmedContext: Both abilities became baseline in the developer overview.

matchups.name: Shaman
matchups.open: Choose an approach that avoids fighting inside a prepared totem position. Identify whether melee pressure or spellcasting is the immediate threat.
matchups.respond: Decide whether removing a particular totem buys more than attacking the player. Keep an interrupt ready for a decisive cast.
matchups.reset: Leave their established field and force a reposition before re-engaging.
matchups.warning: Totems can be deployed and moved more efficiently in Forever. A safe spot can change during the fight.
matchups.confirmedContext: Totemic Projection and Call spells expand totem management.

matchups.name: Mage
matchups.open: Approach from cover with a follow-up route. Preserve a mobility answer for the moment after the opener.
matchups.respond: Watch roots, ranged control and defensive windows. Avoid spending damage cooldowns while the target is protected or unreachable.
matchups.reset: Break sight and recover deliberately. Make the next approach from another angle rather than repeating a losing chase.
matchups.warning: Frostfire Bolt mixes schools and adds a slow and periodic damage. Do not plan solely around old single-school expectations.
matchups.confirmedContext: The developer overview introduces Frostfire Bolt at level 40.

matchups.name: Warlock
matchups.open: Identify the demon and an escape route first. Favor an isolated engagement over a long fight beside enemy reinforcements.
matchups.respond: Treat health, damage-over-time effects and demon control as one resource problem. Interrupt a meaningful cast rather than every available cast.
matchups.reset: Separate from the pet and break sight where possible. Active periodic damage may prevent a clean new Stealth approach.
matchups.warning: Banes are separate from utility Curses, and pets scale from their summoner’s stats. Do not infer an easy target from the old class silhouette.
matchups.confirmedContext: The developer overview confirms Banes and pet scaling.

matchups.name: Druid
matchups.open: Identify form and likely support before choosing pressure or control. Keep enough resources for the shift in the fight after your opener.
matchups.respond: React to the current form instead of assuming a fixed role. Use sight lines to limit recovery and avoid a prolonged unsupported chase.
matchups.reset: Take a favorable disengage and recover; forcing an endless pursuit can cost more than conceding the exchange.
matchups.warning: Druids can use many consumables and weapon effects in form. Old assumptions about forcing them out of form are unsafe.
matchups.confirmedContext: The developer overview expands consumables and weapon procs while shapeshifted.

progression.matchupNote: All nine plans are tactical recommendations, not tested win rates or guaranteed control chains. Numerical beta tuning may have changed after the linked developer overviews.

leveling.title: Deathknell foundations
leveling.plan: Follow the Undead introduction, learn what your current buttons do, and choose safe single pulls. Save money for training and bags.
tasks: Bind movement and the main builder

leveling.title: Build your toolkit
leveling.plan: Finish nearby quest clusters and practice Stealth approaches. Return to training deliberately rather than spending all your coin on short-lived gear.

leveling.title: Leave a safe trail
leveling.plan: Use these as suggested quest hubs, choosing tasks appropriate to your actual level. Collect flight paths and avoid deep caves without an exit.

leveling.title: First dungeon campaign
leveling.plan: Consider a nearby group run when quests and travel make it worthwhile. Compare discovered swords and keep a dagger for your PvP practice.

leveling.title: Contested ground
leveling.plan: These are route options, not a mandatory quest order. Keep an escape route and group when faction traffic makes solo progress expensive.

leveling.title: Make utility your advantage
leveling.plan: Choose quest clusters by enemy level and travel cost. In groups, establish interrupt and control assignments before a difficult pull.

leveling.title: Scout the next campaign
leveling.plan: Finish efficient local objectives before crossing continents. Begin exploring Riverglades as appropriate to quest levels; its announced campaign spans the mid-30s to mid-40s.

leveling.title: Riverglades and two disciplines
leveling.plan: Use Riverglades as a Forever-specific campaign option. At 40, investigate dual specialization and establish separate Combat and Subtlety priorities.

leveling.title: Refine the two loadouts
leveling.plan: Select quests by your client’s levels and local PvP pressure. Reassess Shank at its next rank and compare sword upgrades by actual weapon damage.

leveling.title: Prepare longer expeditions
leveling.plan: These are suggested hubs. Bundle group objectives and avoid expensive detours for a small upgrade when steady quest progress is available.

leveling.title: Turn experience into readiness
leveling.plan: Build a dependable supply routine and record useful high-level groups. Follow current quest markers and tooltips as Forever rewards are discovered.

leveling.title: Arrive prepared
leveling.plan: Choose appropriate final quests and late-level dungeons. Build a verified personal gear list, begin attunement work, and coordinate the December raid schedule.

progression.levelingNote: All twelve bands provide suggested travel and preparation, not a verified quest-by-quest speed route. Exact quest levels, rewards and access should be read in the Forever client. Dungeon ranges are linked separately to official evidence.
progression.macroBoundary: No supplied macro has been live-tested in Forever here. Use conservative commands, label client testing pending, and test target, range, combat and Stealth states before relying on it. Do not promise automated multi-ability sequences or a weapon-swap Ambush shortcut.

presets.title: Combat swords - leveling and PvE starting plan
presets.role: Leveling, dungeons and initial raid preparation
presets.weapons: Main-hand sword; sword off-hand where weapon quality supports it
presets.rationale: Build Combat first: cheaper builders, reliable attacks, a reactive disarm, efficient finishers and sword support. Reach Blade Flurry at baseline level 30 and Adrenaline Rush at 40, then finish Flash of Steel as rank-2 Shank becomes available. Later Assassination points add questing opener value, critical chance and finishing-move support.
caveats: A defensible mixed leveling/PvE plan, not a simulated raid optimum.
Riposte needs a parry and is a solo-melee utility choice; it is not a reliable behind-boss damage button.
Remorseless Attacks favors repeated kills. Raid-only allocation may value different legal points.
Blood Splatter is a flexible long-fight bleed point; it is less useful when the target dies quickly or cannot bleed.
This plan does not take Improved Sprint. The separate PvP plan supplies that root/snare answer.
Shank rank-2 cost and cooldown remain provisional in the data snapshot. Do not advertise exact rank-2 Energy-per-second from this plan.
flexOptions: For a dungeon or raid emphasis, consider a trainer respec from solo parry/kill utility into legal encounter-relevant choices. Revalidate gates after every change.
Maintain Slice and Dice on durable targets and reserve Energy for utility. No preset point total proves an optimal rotation.

presets.title: Subtlety daggers - PvP starting plan
presets.role: World PvP and battleground control with a dagger main hand
presets.weapons: Dagger main hand for Ambush/Backstab; compare useful off-hand properties
presets.rationale: Take the Subtlety capstone first while keeping dagger opener bonuses, cheaper control openers, stealth mobility, reliable Initiative and reset tools. Then buy Improved Sprint and Puncturing Wounds: a root/snare answer and Backstab support suit a dagger Rogue on the PvP ruleset. Malice, longer Gouge and limited Ruthlessness complete a 10/10/31 starting plan.
caveats: An untested control-and-mobility theorycraft; no winrate or damage superiority is claimed.
Master of Deception and Heightened Senses are omitted. Mirror matchups can justify replacing early mobility or damage choices, subject to gates.
This plan trades Lethality and Vigor for Improved Sprint and Puncturing Wounds. A 15/5/31 alternative is a burst-oriented experiment, not an automatic upgrade.
Garrote supplies a bleed, not a verified baseline silence. Bleeds and damaging poisons can prevent damage-sensitive control resets.
Ghostly Strike only waives Stealth for the next Ambush/Garrote within seven seconds; Ambush still needs a main-hand dagger and rear position.
Death Mark is delayed and dispellable as a Curse; whether the full six-second setup will survive is a tactical decision.
flexOptions: For stealth mirrors, test Master of Deception in place of some Opportunity ranks. Both are row 1, so the same five lower-row points remain available.
For enemy detection, test Heightened Senses in place of two lower-tier discretionary ranks only after rechecking that all lower-row gates remain satisfied.
Use control without fresh bleeds when the plan requires Gouge, Blind or a later Sap. A bleed-pressure route makes a different reset tradeoff.

catalogCoverage.scope: Base one-hand swords, daggers, axes, maces and fist weapons, plus ranged bows, guns, crossbows and thrown weapons. Inspected equip requirement at most 60 or not printed; poor through legendary. Inspected equipment restrictions must allow a Horde Rogue. Item statistics come from each item’s own Forever tooltip or an explicitly labeled Classic reference.
catalogCoverage.listingAccess: Direct Wowhead listings returned HTTP 403. Cached listing pages visibly paginate at 50 rows. No capped first-page list is claimed complete; every record of the named source files was considered.
catalogCoverage.enumerationNote: The published caches are finite snapshots, not proof every hidden or unobtainable client item has been discovered. Random suffix families are represented by base item IDs, not every rolled suffix combination.
limitations: Live Forever acquisition and availability are not established by a tooltip. An unconfirmed record may be inaccessible, unreleased or unavailable.
Classic acquisition is labeled separately even when an item has a current Forever tooltip. Classic-only records are reference candidates, not confirmed Forever gear.
Unknown equip requirements stay null and are excluded from usable, near-level and upcoming-level filters.
Phase and source names from Classic cannot establish the Forever release schedule.
Random-suffix families are base item IDs, not every rolled suffix combination.
Armor, two-hand weapons, wands, ammunition, crafting recipes, temporary quest tools, named PTR/debug/NYI items and inspected incompatible class/race restrictions are excluded.
Melee and ranged slots have separate roles. Tooltip DPS sorting does not account for your build, current weapon, special attacks, poison behavior, proc value or encounter.
catalogCoverage.completedScope: All target base-weapon IDs discovered in the three named snapshots were attempted for melee and ranged. Final integration removed 30 recipe wrappers with nested weapon previews and one explicit internal-use test item. This is a broad audited catalog; it is not a claim every possible live or hidden Forever upgrade is known.
catalogCoverage.unavailableFlagCaution: Tooltip API responses do not expose every page-level unavailable/PTR flag. Named debug records, temporary tools, explicit incompatible restrictions and a specifically verified unavailable legendary were excluded. Unknown-source records remain visibly unconfirmed.
catalogCoverage.isHordeAvailabilityNote: isHordeAvailable is null unless a documented Horde source is explicit. No item is promised obtainable solely because it has a tooltip. isHordeUsable describes inspected equipment restrictions, not acquisition.

validation.iconCheck: JPEG headers and SHA-256 match each captured source image

questReferenceEnrichment.note: Quest names and factions are reference acquisition metadata, separate from refreshed Forever item statistics.
